meta.subtitle: How to write a v2 page. Project setup, JSON page structure, rich text, per-page metadata, build outputs. Every section has a real example.
meta.summary: Project setup and page structure — start here.

blocks.summary: A v2 page is one JSON file. Authoring it is filling in a tree of kind-tagged blocks. The HTML stub next to it bootstraps the renderer; you do not edit the HTML.
bullets: Start a new project with html-doc init. Two files per page: name.json (content) and name.html (one-time stub).
The schema is at schema/page.schema.json — VS Code and Cursor autocomplete every node kind.
Rich text inside a paragraph is an array: plain strings interleaved with inline nodes (glossary-term, ext-ref, code, em, strong, link).
Per-page metadata picks accent color, page order in the nav, and the one-line summary that appears in nav tooltips and llms.txt.

blocks.title: Project setup
blocks.lead: One-time per project. Links the kit so pages can reference _kit/chrome.js and friends without copying anything.

blocks.source:
cd ~/path/to/your-project
html-doc init     # creates docs/_kit -> kit symlink

# Optional: copy the starter pair for a blank page
cp ~/dev/mmdemirbas/html-doc/templates/starter.html docs/my-page.html
cp ~/dev/mmdemirbas/html-doc/templates/starter.json docs/my-page.json

html-doc serve    # opens in the browser

content: After init, your project has a

blocks.title: kit.json — declare your project
blocks.content: Each project's docs/kit.json picks which glossary domains to activate, the preferred language, and any project-local glossary or ext-ref overrides. The kit ships starter domains (data-platforms, web, ai-llm) — pick whichever fit. The glossary page covers domain selection in detail.

blocks.title: Anatomy of a page
blocks.lead: Every JSON page is rooted at kind:"page" and has three pieces: title, meta, blocks.

items: and the H1 in the cover.
) or a CSS color value. Overrides the kit default per page.
— optional object. eyebrow, subtitle, audience, date, read_time, order, summary, lang. Each is optional individually.
— the content tree. Array of top-level blocks (tldr, kpi-grid, section).

content.content: meta.summary is surfaced in three places: the page-nav tooltip on hover, the llms.txt sitemap line for AI consumers, and (when present) the Pagefind search excerpt. Keep it one tight sentence focused on what the page contains — not a teaser.

blocks.title: Block kinds
blocks.lead: Each block in the tree has a kind tag the renderer matches to a renderer function (or, for the visual primitives, a Custom Element). The primitives reference page lists every kind with a live example.

content: Two levels:
allowed only at the page root (tldr, kpi-grid, section), and
allowed inside section.blocks (paragraph, heading, callout, insight, info-tip, list, code, plus all the visual primitives).

cards.title: Top-level only
content: tldr — the highlighted opener box (label, summary, bullets).
kpi-grid — headline-number tiles.
section — every chunk of real content lives in a section so the TOC builds from it.

cards.title: Inside section.blocks
content: paragraph, heading, list, code — prose primitives.
callout, insight, info-tip — emphasis primitives.
kpi-grid, compare-grid, scope-grid — structured layout primitives.
bar-chart, step-flow, chart, diagram, live-snippet — visual primitives.

blocks.title: Section IDs are required
blocks.content: Every section needs an id. The TOC, scroll-spy, and section permalinks all key off it. Use kebab-case; the kit doesn't sanitize.

blocks.title: Rich text — strings or arrays
blocks.lead: Anywhere the schema accepts text (paragraph content, callout content, list items, etc.), you can pass a string for plain prose or an array to mix inline nodes.

items: — { kind, term, text?, in?, lang? }. Resolves against the active glossary domains.
— { kind, name, text?, in?, lang? }. Like glossary-term but for external entities.
— { kind, text, href }. External links get target=_blank automatically.

content: Inline nodes can appear in any place the schema marks as
— paragraph.content, list.items[*], callout.content, insight.content, info-tip nested paragraphs, compare-card.content, scope-col.items[*], step-card.content, and tldr.bullets[*].

blocks.title: Per-page metadata
blocks.lead: meta drives nav placement, the cover header, the llms.txt sitemap, and search excerpts.

cards.title: Display fields
content: eyebrow — small label above the H1 ("Architecture", "Notes").
subtitle — one-paragraph description under the H1.
audience — "Spark+Iceberg team", "Personal", etc.
date — ISO date or human string. Shown in cover meta.
read_time — like "~5 min read". Shown in cover meta.

cards.title: Behavior fields
content: order — sort key in the site-tree nav. Lower = earlier.
summary — one line. Used in nav tooltips, llms.txt, search.
lang — "en" or "tr" (or any code the kit knows). Overrides the project default.
accent (top-level, not under meta) — named token or CSS color.

content.content: The kit doesn't parse the date — it's a display string. Use whatever convention you've adopted (ISO 8601, locale date). For consistency across a project, pick one and stick. Sort order in the nav uses meta.order, not the date.

blocks.title: Build outputs
blocks.lead: html-doc build produces four artifacts. Authors don't need to run it during dev — the runtime renderer fetches JSON directly — but build is required for search, the standalone single-file mode, and the llms.txt sitemap.

steps.title: site-manifest.json
steps.content: Page tree consumed by the site-tree sidebar at runtime. Generated from every *.json file in the project.

steps.title: llms.txt
steps.content: One line per page: URL + title + summary. Convention from llmstxt.org. Drop into LLM context to give the model an overview.

steps.title: dist/site/
steps.content: Every HTML + JSON copied with directory structure preserved. Kit assets bundled at dist/site/_kit/. Drop on any static host.

steps.title: dist/standalone/
steps.content: Every HTML inlined: kit JS, CSS, page JSON, glossary bundle. One self-contained file per page that opens offline — email-as-attachment ready.

blocks.title: Pagefind search — optional dependency
blocks.content: If pagefind is on PATH (brew install pagefind, or npx pagefind), build also indexes dist/site/ into dist/site/pagefind/. Soft-fails without it. The search button in the chrome only works on built sites.
